profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, VA1, is located at 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive, Reston, VA 20191, part of CoreSite's three-building Reston campus alongside VA2 and VA3. CoreSite publishes 261,000-plus square feet for VA1 on the main facility page; the operator's spec-sheet landing page instead cites a forward-looking campus total of "more than 1.3 million square feet of colocation space upon full build out," and the VA1 page separately describes the three-building campus as totaling "over 986,000 square feet" today, two different campus-wide figures that do not reconcile with each other. No MW capacity or opening year is stated for VA1 specifically; the operator cites N+2 generator redundancy for the campus. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to this Reston campus. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class for data centers effective January 1, 2027, under which facilities with 25 megawatts or more of demand face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements, per Inside Climate News.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across the Reston campus among CoreSite's other markets.

profile.capacity_note: not published by the operator at the building level. No reliable MW or power figure found in any aggregator source checked this session either.
profile.research_note: CoreSite publishes three different campus-wide sqft totals across its own pages (986,000+ current; 940,000+ on VA3's spec sheet; 1.3 million "upon full build out" on VA1's spec sheet) -- flagged rather than reconciled, since these appear to mix current and planned figures.
sources_tried: CoreSites own Northern Virginia regional page and dedicated VA1 spec sheet page, plus a DataCenterMap aggregator listing found to be internally inconsistent on square footage and therefore not relied upon
profile.square_footage: 261,000+ sq ft (operator figure). A third-party aggregator shows two mutually inconsistent figures for the same address, 201,000 and 188,000 sq ft, neither trusted over the operators own number.

reading.body:
CoreSite Reston Campus VA1 is a 261,000 square foot facility in Reston, Virginia with no published power capacity figure available from the operator or other sources checked. Without a megawatt specification, the campus cannot be assessed as to the absolute scale of AI infrastructure it can support, making comparison to other facilities by compute density impossible at this stage. The operator's specification sheet and regional page do not disclose power capacity for this building.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities total, of which 23 publish power figures. The state's published total capacity across those 23 facilities is 1,375 megawatts. CoreSite Reston Campus VA1 is not among those 23 published facilities, placing it outside the ranked set by power disclosure. Its rank cannot be determined without a power figure.

The adjacent Reston campus building VA3 carries NVIDIA DGX-Ready certification, indicating it qualifies to host NVIDIA GPU clusters for training workloads. Whether VA1 holds similar qualification or certification is not published. Until the operator publishes power capacity for VA1, the facility cannot be read as a material constraint or contributor to AI scaling on the Virginia grid.
